data.title: Charts are hand-written inline SVG, with no chart library and no script
data.why: The export's one promise is that the page asks the network for nothing, and the test asserts it structurally: no script tag, no link, no url(), no https anywhere. Every chart library is a script tag, so the choice was between a library and the promise. Hand-drawn SVG measured 0.1 ms and 14 KB for the flow page and 1.7 ms and 301 KB for a two-year cumulative flow diagram - both a fraction of the 200 ms budget. Inline SVG also needs no xmlns, which is the only reason it can pass the no-network test at all.
data.rejected: Chart.js or uPlot from a CDN, which is a network request at open time; a bundled copy of a library, which is a script tag either way; a rendered PNG, which needs a headless browser as a dependency; the div-width bars the burndown uses, which cannot draw a seven-band cumulative flow
